blocks.description: Opening frame: search declines are usually misdiagnosed; at A Place for Mom the decline was equal parts content problem and architecture problem.

lengths.full:
Search declines get misdiagnosed for a living. The rankings slip, someone blames the content, someone else blames the algorithm, and the real problem sits underneath both.

At A Place for Mom it was both: equal parts content problem and architecture problem. Treating it as one or the other would have fixed half of it. What follows is the diagnosis and what it produced.

blocks.description: Practice, AI readiness and answer discoverability: whether AI engines can find a brand, understand what it offers, and represent it accurately.

lengths.compact: Answer discoverability is whether an AI engine can find your brand, understand what you offer, and represent you accurately when a customer asks it a question, both when someone asks about you by name and when the question is about your category.
lengths.full:
Answer discoverability is whether an AI engine can find your brand, understand what you offer, and represent you accurately when a customer asks it a question. It has two layers: the engine has to get you right when someone asks about you by name, and it has to name you when the question is about your category and nobody gave it your name.

Those are different tests, and a brand can pass some and fail others: whether the engine can retrieve the information at all, whether it identifies the right entity, whether it understands the information accurately, whether it cites or recommends the source, and whether what it has is current.

His published formulation is that GEO and AEO are not new disciplines. They are new front doors into the same business of being found and understood. The fundamentals did not change. The surfacing did. The tradeoff is real: an engine can make a brand visible without sending it a visit, and deciding what that visibility is worth, then measuring it on its own terms, is part of the work.

blocks.description: Practice, composable martech and customer data: best-of-breed tools connected through defined contracts, and what a CDP is in his framing.

lengths.full: Composable martech is a stack built from best-of-breed tools, each chosen for one job and connected through defined interfaces, instead of a single vendor suite. The content platform, the data platform, the decisioning tools, and the analytics layer are separate components with clean contracts between them: documented schemas, stable interfaces, clear ownership. When one component stops earning its place, you can replace that component without rebuilding the whole stack, and you do not wait for a suite vendor’s roadmap to catch up with your business.

blocks.description: Practice, digital experience strategy: deciding what a brand's websites and apps should do, then building toward it across channels.

lengths.full:
Digital experience strategy is the work of deciding what a brand’s website and apps should do, then building the team and the data to do it. The deliverable is not a deck. It is one set of metrics that matter, one shared understanding of the customer, and a sequence the organization can actually execute: what gets built, in what order, and how everyone will know it worked.

Technology decisions are only part of the strategy. The harder work is deciding what matters first, who owns it, what the organization can deliver, and how progress will be measured.

blocks.description: Practice, experimentation and measurement: tests that state a hypothesis and one primary metric, and reporting that ties results to business outcomes.

lengths.full:
Experimentation is how an organization finds out whether a change worked. A test states a hypothesis, names one primary metric before it runs, and reads the result against that metric, which means the tests aim at a specific outcome and the decisioning is built to test against the objective, not the screen.

None of that holds without the layer underneath: events defined the same way by every team, metrics that mean the same thing in every dashboard, and readouts people trust enough to act on. Measurement is the precondition. Shared KPIs, shared language, governance and reporting, agreed before the tooling arguments start.

blocks.description: Principles: gates, not prompts; the harness checks and the approval rule behind the work.

lengths.full:
Gates, not prompts. A prompt is a request; a gate is a control.

The harness checks are Brand Out-of-Bounds, Contextual Switch, and Guardrails. A prompt is a request; a gate is a control.

Nothing on douglascirillo.com publishes without Douglas Cirillo's approval. Every draft comes back to him; he edits, decides, and approves.
